explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/713 (Erdős–Simonovits): is it true that for every bipartite G there exist α ∈ [1,2) and c > 0 with ex(n;G) ∼ cn^α? The Lean statement quantifies over bipartite G on Fin q with at least two edges and asks for α ∈ Ico 1 2, c > 0 with extremalNumber n G ∼ c n^α (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent). The ≥ 2 edges restriction only removes graphs with ≤ 1 edge, whose extremal number is eventually 0 and for which c > 0 is impossible — a necessary exclusion of trivial counterexamples (e.g. 2K₂ and P₃ have ex ∼ n and ∼ n/2, so the remaining cases behave as intended). Isolated vertices in G do not affect ex(n;G) for large n. Positive form per the question convention. Faithful.
